title: Independent expressions
description: (a + b) XOR (a − b), with 32-bit wrapping.
source: (module (func (export "run") (param $a i32) (param $b i32) (result i32) (i32.xor (i32.add (local.get $a) (local.get $b)) (i32.sub (local.get $a) (local.get $b)))))

title: Wrapping addition
description: Add two i32 integers. Try 4294967295 + 1.
source:
(module
  (func (export "add")
    (param $a i32) (param $b i32) (result i32)
    local.get $a
    local.get $b
    i32.add
  )
)

title: 64-bit expressions
description: The same expression with full 64-bit integers.
source: (module (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64) (result i64) (i64.xor (i64.add (local.get $a) (local.get $b)) (i64.sub (local.get $a) (local.get $b)))))

title: Two 64-bit dividers + addition
description: Compute (a / b) + (c / d) with independent signed i64 dividers and wrapping addition. Division truncates toward zero; either division can trap.
source:
;; Two independent full-width signed dividers compose with wrapping addition.
;; All four operands are supplied at invocation time.
(module
  (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64)
                      (param $c i64) (param $d i64) (result i64)
    local.get $a local.get $b i64.div_s
    local.get $c local.get $d i64.div_s
    i64.add))

title: Two 64-bit divisions → multiplication
description: Compute (a / b) × (c / d) with unsigned i64 division and a wrapping product. Both runtime quotients feed the multiplier; either zero divisor traps.
source:
;; Three expensive runtime operations in one font: two divisions, then multiply.
;; The product wraps modulo 2^64; either zero divisor traps.
(module
  (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64)
                      (param $c i64) (param $d i64) (result i64)
    local.get $a local.get $b i64.div_u
    local.get $c local.get $d i64.div_u
    i64.mul))

title: Signed divisions → multiply → count bits
description: Return (a / b) × (c / d) and its set-bit count. Four runtime operations compose with signed i64 division and wrapping multiplication. Either zero divisor or MIN / −1 traps.
source:
;; Four runtime operations: two signed divisions, multiplication, and popcount.
;; Return the wrapping product and its number of set bits.
(module
  (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64)
                      (param $c i64) (param $d i64) (result i64 i64)
    (local $product i64)
    local.get $a local.get $b i64.div_s
    local.get $c local.get $d i64.div_s
    i64.mul local.tee $product
    local.get $product i64.popcnt))

title: Three 64-bit dividers + addition
description: Compute (a / b) + (c / d) + (e / f) with three independent unsigned i64 dividers and wrapping addition. Any zero divisor traps.
source:
;; Three independent dynamic full-width dividers, combined with wrapping adds.
;; Any zero divisor traps.
(module
  (func (export "run") (param i64 i64 i64 i64 i64 i64) (result i64)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u
    local.get 2 local.get 3 i64.div_u i64.add
    local.get 4 local.get 5 i64.div_u i64.add))

title: Four 64-bit dividers + addition
description: Compute (a / b) + (c / d) + (e / f) + (g / h) with four independent unsigned i64 dividers and wrapping addition. Any zero divisor traps.
source:
;; Four independent dynamic full-width unsigned dividers with wrapping sums.
;; Any zero divisor traps.
(module
  (func (export "run") (param i64 i64 i64 i64 i64 i64 i64 i64) (result i64)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u
    local.get 2 local.get 3 i64.div_u i64.add
    local.get 4 local.get 5 i64.div_u i64.add
    local.get 6 local.get 7 i64.div_u i64.add))

title: Conditional branch
description: Return a − b when a < b (signed); otherwise a + b.
source: (module (func (export "run") (param i32) (param i32) (result i32) (if (result i32) (i32.lt_s (local.get 0) (local.get 1)) (then (i32.sub (local.get 0) (local.get 1))) (else (i32.add (local.get 0) (local.get 1))))))

title: Bounded loop
description: Sum n down to 1. Inputs 0–7 finish; 8 reaches the loop bound.
source:
(module (func (export "run") (param $n i32) (result i32) (local $sum i32)
 block $done loop $again local.get $n i32.eqz br_if $done
 local.get $sum local.get $n i32.add local.set $sum
 local.get $n i32.const 1 i32.sub local.set $n br $again end end local.get $sum))

title: Recursive calls
description: Sum n down to 1 using internal calls. Inputs 0–7 fit the call bound.
source: (module (func $f (export "run") (param $n i32) (result i32) (if (result i32) (i32.eqz (local.get $n)) (then (i32.const 0)) (else (i32.add (local.get $n) (call $f (i32.sub (local.get $n) (i32.const 1))))))))

title: Memory round trip
description: Store and load a 32-bit value. Addresses 0–12 fit the backed window.
source: (module (memory 1) (func (export "run") (param $addr i32) (param $value i32) (result i32) local.get $addr local.get $value i32.store local.get $addr i32.load))

title: 64-bit division → typed loop
description: Divide a / b once, then carry the quotient and remainder through a loop: add the remainder to the checksum and increment it each round. Rounds 0–7 finish; 8 reaches the loop bound. A zero divisor traps.
source:
(module
  (type $carry (func (param i32 i64 i64) (result i64 i64)))
  (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64) (param $rounds i32)
    (result i64 i64) (local $n i32) (local $checksum i64) (local $remainder i64)
    ;; A multi-value block produces the full-width quotient and remainder.
    block (result i64 i64)
      local.get $a local.get $b i64.div_u
      local.get $a local.get $b i64.rem_u
    end
    local.set $remainder local.set $checksum
    local.get $rounds local.get $checksum local.get $remainder
    ;; Each backedge carries (rounds left, checksum, remainder) on the stack.
    loop $again (type $carry)
      local.set $remainder local.set $checksum local.tee $n i32.eqz
      if (result i64 i64)
        local.get $checksum local.get $remainder
      else
        local.get $n i32.const 1 i32.sub
        local.get $checksum local.get $remainder i64.add
        local.get $remainder i64.const 1 i64.add
        br $again
      end
    end))

title: Memory fill + overlapping copy
description: Store the seed in bytes 0–7, fill bytes 8–15 with the low byte of the fill value, then copy length bytes from source to destination. Overlaps preserve the original source bytes. Both ranges must fit the 16-byte window unless length is zero.
source:
(module
  (memory 1)
  (func (export "run") (param $seed i64) (param $destination i32)
    (param $source i32) (param $length i32) (param $byte i32) (result i64 i64)
    ;; Initialize eight bytes from the seed, then fill the next eight bytes.
    i32.const 0 local.get $seed i64.store
    i32.const 8 local.get $byte i32.const 8 memory.fill
    ;; Copy from a snapshot, including when source and destination overlap.
    local.get $destination local.get $source local.get $length memory.copy
    ;; Return the entire 16-byte window as two little-endian i64 values.
    i32.const 0 i64.load
    i32.const 8 i64.load))

title: Passive data → memory
description: Copy bytes from an embedded segment containing 1–16 into the zeroed 16-byte memory window, then drop the segment. Set drop first to 1 to discard it before the copy; only length 0 at source 0 then succeeds.
source:
(module
  (memory 1)
  ;; Passive data remains separate from linear memory until memory.init runs.
  (data $bytes "\01\02\03\04\05\06\07\08\09\0a\0b\0c\0d\0e\0f\10")
  (func (export "run") (param $destination i32) (param $source i32)
    (param $length i32) (param $drop_first i32) (result i64 i64)
    local.get $drop_first
    if data.drop $bytes end
    local.get $destination local.get $source local.get $length memory.init $bytes
    ;; Dropping the segment preserves bytes already copied into memory.
    data.drop $bytes
    i32.const 0 i64.load
    i32.const 8 i64.load))

title: Grow memory in the font
description: Start with one page, store the value, then attempt two growth steps up to a maximum of three pages. Each step returns the previous page count or −1 on failure; failed growth preserves the memory size and stored value.
source:
(module
  ;; Growth changes the logical page count; memory starts with one 64-KiB page.
  (memory 1 3)
  (func (export "run") (param $first i32) (param $second i32)
    (param $value i64) (result i32 i32 i32 i64)
    ;; Existing bytes survive successful and failed growth attempts.
    i32.const 0 local.get $value i64.store
    local.get $first memory.grow
    local.get $second memory.grow
    memory.size
    i32.const 0 i64.load))

title: Initialize before the export
description: A start function grows memory, copies seed bytes 1–16, drops the seed segment, and increments an initialization counter before run changes one byte. Addresses 0–15 fit the backed window. Each run starts with a fresh initialized module.
source:
(module
  (memory 0 1)
  (data $seed "\01\02\03\04\05\06\07\08\09\0a\0b\0c\0d\0e\0f\10")
  (global $starts (mut i32) (i32.const 0))
  ;; Instantiation initializes the memory before run receives its arguments.
  (start $initialize)
  (func $initialize
    i32.const 1 memory.grow drop
    i32.const 0 i32.const 0 i32.const 16 memory.init $seed
    data.drop $seed
    global.get $starts i32.const 1 i32.add global.set $starts)
  (func (export "run") (param $address i32) (param $value i32)
    (result i64 i64 i32 i32)
    local.get $address local.get $value i32.store8
    i32.const 0 i64.load i32.const 8 i64.load
    memory.size global.get $starts))

title: Computed module initialization
description: Compute the seed address and divisor with constant expressions, seed the callback table directly, then replace a callback using an immutable global. Operation 0 adds the embedded 64-bit seed; operation 1 XORs with the seed and divides unsigned by seven. Other operation indices trap.
source:
(module
  (memory 1)
  (table $operations 2 funcref (ref.func $add_seed))
  (global $base i32 (i32.mul (i32.const 2) (i32.const 4)))
  (global $divisor i64 (i64.sub (i64.const 10) (i64.const 3)))
  (global $divide funcref (ref.func $divide_seed))
  ;; Place the seed at byte 8 and replace table slot 1 with division.
  (data (offset (global.get $base) (i32.const 0) i32.add)
    "\01\02\03\04\05\06\07\08")
  (elem (table $operations)
    (i32.sub (global.get $base) (i32.const 7)) funcref
    (item (global.get $divide)))
  (func $add_seed (param i64) (result i64)
    local.get 0 global.get $base i64.load i64.add)
  (func $divide_seed (param i64) (result i64)
    local.get 0 global.get $base i64.load i64.xor
    global.get $divisor i64.div_u)
  (func (export "run") (param $value i64) (param $operation i32) (result i64)
    local.get $value local.get $operation
    call_indirect $operations (param i64) (result i64)))

title: Choose a 64-bit function at runtime
description: Select addition (0), subtraction (1), multiplication (2), or unsigned division (3), then count the result’s set bits. Slot 4 has the wrong signature, slot 5 is null, and indices 6+ are out of bounds. Only the selected function can trap.
source:
(module
  (type $binary (func (param i64 i64) (result i64)))
  (table $operations 6 funcref)
  ;; Slots 0–3 select arithmetic; slot 4 has the wrong type; slot 5 is null.
  (elem (i32.const 0) $add $subtract $multiply $divide $wrong_type)
  (func $add (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add)
  (func $subtract (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.sub)
  (func $multiply (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.mul)
  (func $divide (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u)
  (func $wrong_type (param i32) (result i32) local.get 0)
  (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64) (param $operation i32)
    (result i64 i64) (local $result i64)
    local.get $a local.get $b local.get $operation call_indirect $operations (type $binary)
    ;; The selected function's result feeds more Wasm instructions in this font.
    local.tee $result local.get $result i64.popcnt))

title: Change and grow a function table
description: Copy addition and unsigned division from a passive segment, drop the segment, select a function reference, replace slot 0 and grow a new slot with it. Call the new slot and count the result’s bits. Operation 0 adds; 1 divides; other indices trap.
source:
;; Populate a passive function segment, mutate a slot and grow the table.
(module
  (type $binary (func (param i64 i64) (result i64)))
  (table $ops 2 3 funcref)
  (elem $functions func $add $divide)
  (func $add (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add)
  (func $divide (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u)
  (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64) (param $operation i32)
    (result i64 i64 i32) (local $chosen funcref) (local $answer i64)
    i32.const 0 i32.const 0 i32.const 2 table.init $ops $functions
    elem.drop $functions
    local.get $operation table.get $ops local.set $chosen
    i32.const 0 local.get $chosen table.set $ops
    local.get $chosen i32.const 1 table.grow $ops drop
    local.get $a local.get $b i32.const 2 call_indirect $ops (type $binary)
    local.tee $answer local.get $answer i64.popcnt table.size $ops))

title: Copy callbacks between tables
description: Copy a selected callback from a library into a separate dispatch table, grow that table with the callback, then call the new slot. Operation 0 adds, 1 XORs, and 2 divides unsigned i64 values. Other indices trap. The library stays at three slots while the dispatch table grows from one to two.
source:
;; Copy one callback from a library into a separate, growing dispatch table.
(module
  (type $binary (func (param i64 i64) (result i64)))
  (table $library 3 3 funcref)
  (table $dispatch 1 2 funcref)
  (elem (i32.const 0) $add $xor $divide)
  (func $add (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add)
  (func $xor (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.xor)
  (func $divide (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u)
  (func (export "run") (param i64 i64 i32) (result i64 i32 i32)
    i32.const 0 local.get 2 i32.const 1 table.copy $dispatch $library
    i32.const 0 table.get $dispatch i32.const 1 table.grow $dispatch drop
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i32.const 1 call_indirect $dispatch (type $binary)
    table.size $library table.size $dispatch))

title: 64-bit division → tail recursion
description: Divide once, then add the remainder into the checksum and increment it each round. Direct and indirect tail calls reuse one call frame. Rounds 0–7 fit the eight-transition tail budget; 8 reports a tail-call bound. A zero divisor traps before recursion.
source:
;; Divide once, then carry quotient and remainder through tail-recursive rounds.
(module
  (table $unused 0 funcref)
  (table $steps 1 funcref)
  (elem (table $steps) (i32.const 0) $advance)
  (func $advance (param i64 i64 i32) (result i64 i64)
    local.get 2 if (result i64 i64)
      local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add
      local.get 1 i64.const 1 i64.add
      local.get 2 i32.const 1 i32.sub
      i32.const 0 return_call_indirect $steps (param i64 i64 i32) (result i64 i64)
    else local.get 0 local.get 1 end)
  (func (export "run") (param i64 i64 i32) (result i64 i64)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.rem_u
    local.get 2 return_call $advance))

title: Pass function references through helpers
description: Choose a nullable table reference or fallback addition, pass it through a helper and typed block, store it in a mutable global, then dispatch and count bits. Slots 0 and 2 add or divide; slot 1 is null. Set use selected slot to 0 for fallback addition; the slot must still be in bounds.
source:
;; Nullable references move through a typed select, helper, block and global.
(module
  (type $binary (func (param i64 i64) (result i64)))
  (table 3 funcref)
  (elem (i32.const 0) funcref (ref.func $add) (ref.null func) (ref.func $divide))
  (global $chosen (mut funcref) (ref.null func))
  (func $add (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add)
  (func $divide (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u)
  (func $choose (param funcref funcref i32) (result funcref)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 local.get 2 select (result funcref))
  (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64) (param $slot i32) (param $use_slot i32)
    (result i64 i64) (local $answer i64)
    local.get $slot table.get ref.func $add local.get $use_slot call $choose
    block (param funcref) (result funcref) end global.set $chosen
    i32.const 1 global.get $chosen table.set
    local.get $a local.get $b i32.const 1 call_indirect (type $binary)
    local.tee $answer local.get $answer i64.popcnt))

title: Optional callback or strict null check
description: Choose addition (slot 0), an empty callback (slot 1), or unsigned 64-bit division (slot 2). With strict set to 0, a null-reference branch chooses fallback addition. With strict set to 1, a null callback traps before dispatch. The chosen reference passes through a helper into a separate table.
source:
(module
  (table $callbacks 3 funcref)
  (table $dispatch 1 funcref)
  (elem (table $callbacks) (i32.const 0) $add)
  (elem (table $callbacks) (i32.const 2) $divide)
  (func $add (param i64 i64) (result i64)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add)
  (func $divide (param i64 i64) (result i64)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u)
  (func $choose (param $candidate funcref) (param $strict i32) (result funcref)
    local.get $strict
    if (result funcref)
      local.get $candidate ref.as_non_null
    else
      block $found (result funcref)
        local.get $candidate br_on_non_null $found
        ref.func $add
      end
    end)
  (func (export "run") (param $a i64) (param $b i64)
    (param $slot i32) (param $strict i32) (result i64)
    ;; Keep the operands below the callback-selection work on the stack.
    local.get $a local.get $b
    i32.const 0
    local.get $slot table.get $callbacks local.get $strict call $choose
    table.set $dispatch
    i32.const 0 call_indirect $dispatch (param i64 i64) (result i64)))

title: Call typed callbacks without a table
description: Pass a typed function reference through a helper and call it directly. Operation 0 adds, 1 XORs, and 2 divides unsigned i64 values. Operation 3 selects null and traps at call_ref; other indices trap while selecting the callback.
source:
(module
  (type $binary (func (param i64 i64) (result i64)))
  (global $add (ref $binary) (ref.func $add))
  (global $xor (ref $binary) (ref.func $xor))
  (global $divide (ref $binary) (ref.func $divide))
  (func $add (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add)
  (func $xor (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.xor)
  (func $divide (type $binary) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u)
  (func $choose (param $operation i32) (result (ref null $binary))
    local.get $operation i32.const 3 i32.gt_u if unreachable end
    local.get $operation i32.const 3 i32.eq
    if (result (ref null $binary))
      ref.null $binary
    else
      local.get $operation i32.eqz
      if (result (ref $binary)) global.get $add
      else
        local.get $operation i32.const 1 i32.eq
        if (result (ref $binary)) global.get $xor else global.get $divide end
      end
    end)
  (func (export "run") (param i64 i64 i32) (result i64)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 local.get 2 call $choose call_ref $binary))

title: 64-bit division → reference tail calls
description: Divide once, then carry the quotient and remainder through reference tail calls in one frame. Each round adds the remainder to the checksum and increments it. Rounds 0–7 fit the eight-transition tail budget; 8 reports a tail-call bound.
source:
(module
  (type $step (func (param i32 i64 i64) (result i64 i64)))
  (elem declare func $step)
  (func $step (type $step)
    local.get 0
    if (result i64 i64)
      local.get 0 i32.const 1 i32.sub
      local.get 1 local.get 2 i64.add
      local.get 2 i64.const 1 i64.add
      ref.func $step return_call_ref $step
    else local.get 1 local.get 2 end)
  (func (export "run") (param $dividend i64) (param $divisor i64)
    (param $rounds i32) (result i64 i64)
    local.get $rounds
    local.get $dividend local.get $divisor i64.div_u
    local.get $dividend local.get $divisor i64.rem_u
    ref.func $step return_call_ref $step))

title: Grow and call a non-null typed table
description: Read a typed callback from a non-null library, grow a separate typed dispatch table with it, then tail-call the new slot directly. Operation 0 adds, 1 XORs, and 2 divides unsigned i64 values. Other indices trap. Returns the selected result and the two-slot dispatch size.
source:
(module
  (type $binary (func (param i64 i64) (result i64 i32)))
  (table $library 3 (ref $binary) (ref.func $add))
  (table $dispatch 1 2 (ref $binary) (ref.func $add))
  (elem (table $library) (i32.const 1) (ref $binary)
    (ref.func $xor) (ref.func $divide))
  (func $add (type $binary)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add table.size $dispatch)
  (func $xor (type $binary)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.xor table.size $dispatch)
  (func $divide (type $binary)
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.div_u table.size $dispatch)
  (func (export "run") (param i64 i64 i32) (result i64 i32)
    local.get 2 table.get $library i32.const 1 table.grow $dispatch drop
    local.get 0 local.get 1 i32.const 1 table.get $dispatch
    return_call_ref $binary))

title: Indexed byte in a 64-byte window
description: Store an i64 seed at bytes 32–39, then read a byte at a runtime offset and count the seed’s set bits. Offsets 0–63 fit the backed window; higher valid Wasm addresses report a memory bound.
source:
;; A runtime i64 store and byte lookup in a 64-byte window.
(module
  (memory 1)
  (data (i32.const 0)
    "\01\12\23\34\45\56\67\78\89\9a\ab\bc\cd\de\ef\f0"
    "\10\21\32\43\54\65\76\87\98\a9\ba\cb\dc\ed\fe\0f"
    "\20\31\42\53\64\75\86\97\a8\b9\ca\db\ec\fd\0e\1f"
    "\30\41\52\63\74\85\96\a7\b8\c9\da\eb\fc\0d\1e\2f")
  (func (export "run") (param $offset i32) (param $seed i64) (result i32 i64)
    i32.const 32 local.get $seed i64.store
    local.get $offset i32.load8_u
    local.get $seed i64.popcnt))

title: Indexed words → 64-bit arithmetic
description: Fill a 64-byte buffer from two runtime seeds, read two unaligned i64 words, then return their wrapping sum and their XOR divided by the unsigned divisor. Offsets 0–56 fit the backed window. Shared wide reads leave room for the divider within an 8,000-gate construction budget.
source:
;; Fill a 64-byte runtime buffer, read two unaligned words, then compose them.
(module (memory 1)
  (func (export "run") (param i64 i64 i32 i32 i64) (result i64 i64) (local i64 i64)
    i32.const 0 local.get 0 i64.store
    i32.const 8 local.get 1 i64.store
    i32.const 16 local.get 0 i64.const 8 i64.rotl i64.store
    i32.const 24 local.get 1 i64.const -1 i64.xor i64.store
    i32.const 32 local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.add i64.store
    i32.const 40 local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.xor i64.store
    i32.const 48 local.get 1 i64.const 32 i64.rotl i64.store
    i32.const 56 local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.sub i64.store
    local.get 2 i64.load local.set 5
    local.get 3 i64.load local.set 6
    local.get 5 local.get 6 i64.add
    local.get 5 local.get 6 i64.xor local.get 4 i64.div_u))

title: Unsigned division
description: Divide two i32 values. A zero divisor produces a Wasm trap.
source: (module (func (export "run") (param i32 i32) (result i32) local.get 0 local.get 1 i32.div_u))

title: 64-bit division by 10
description: Return the unsigned quotient and remainder of a full-width i64 value divided by ten.
source:
(module
  (func (export "run") (param $value i64) (result i64 i64)

title: 64-bit signed division by −7
description: Return the signed quotient and remainder. Division truncates toward zero; remainder keeps the input sign.
source:
(module
  (func (export "run") (param $value i64) (result i64 i64)
    ;; Division truncates toward zero; remainder keeps the dividend's sign.
    local.get $value
    i64.const -7
    i64.div_s
    local.get $value
    i64.const -7
    i64.rem_s))

title: Dynamic 64-bit division
description: Return unsigned quotient and remainder for two full-width i64 arguments. A zero divisor traps.
source:
(module
  (func (export "run") (param $dividend i64) (param $divisor i64) (result i64 i64)
    local.get $dividend
    local.get $divisor
    i64.div_u
    local.get $dividend
    local.get $divisor
    i64.rem_u))

title: 64-bit multiplication
description: Multiply arbitrary i64 values with wrapping.
source: (module (func (export "run") (param i64 i64) (result i64) local.get 0 local.get 1 i64.mul))

title: Count set bits
description: Count the set bits in an i64 integer, then add three.
source:
(module
  (func (export "run") (param $x i64) (result i64)
    local.get $x
    i64.popcnt
    i64.const 3
    i64.add))

title: Compiled C · array loop
description: Add bias to the first count elements of [3, 5, 7, 11], then return their sum with unsigned 32-bit wrapping. Counts 0–4 succeed; other counts trap. The compiled loop reads and writes a 16-byte window at address 65536. Each run starts with the original array.

title: Compiled C · stack and globals
description: Read the first count globals from [3, 5, 7, 11], add bias into a local stack array and sum it in another function. Counts 0–4 succeed. Two 16-byte regions back the stack and globals across a 496-byte gap.

title: Compiled C · function pointers
description: Load a volatile C function pointer and pass it to a non-inlined helper. Operation 0 adds, 1 XORs, and 2 divides full-width unsigned i64 inputs. Other operations trap. A zero divisor traps only for operation 2.

title: Compiled C · tail-call callbacks
description: The callback C source compiled with -mtail-call: run tail-calls its helper, which tail-calls the selected function pointer. Both calls reuse one frame. Operation 0 adds, 1 XORs, and 2 divides unsigned i64 inputs; other operations trap.

title: Compiled C · packet checksum
description: Copy 0–7 payload bytes from an embedded packet into a local stack buffer, add the adjustment to each byte, then compute a 32-bit rolling checksum in a helper. Counts above the packet header’s limit trap; each invocation starts fresh.
